INVESTIGATIONS OF SYSTEMIC LUPUS ERYTHEMATOSUS
Investigations
- Haematocrit, white blood cell count, platelet count
- ESR, CRP . ESR markedly high while CRP is normal or marginally raised.
Markedly elevated ESR may be suggestive of SLE if other conditions
causing this have been eliminated. This is in lieu of serologies especially in
patients who cannot afford the latter.
- Urine analysis and microscopy – for casts, RBCs, protein
- Electrolytes and urea
- Chest X-ray, ECG
- Serology – Anti–nuclear Antibody (ANA); Extractable Nuclear Antigen
(ENA); Double stranded DNA
- Kidney Biopsy – as indicated
